candidates.exact_span: The draft permit proposes E. coli limits consistently with the approved TMDL.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of how E. coli limits align with the approved TMDL could change which enforceable numeric E. coli limit is selected for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The standard reopener language in the permit allows additional permit conditions if warranted by future changes and/or new TMDLs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether reopener language is treated as presently operative or as reserving only future conditions could change which limits and monitoring requirements are considered applicable during FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The limitations and monitoring requirements set forth in the proposed draft are developed from the appropriate State WQS and are protective of those designated uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which limits and monitoring obligations are WQS-derived versus report-only could change applicable numeric limits (A), which monitoring requirements are in force (B), and how missing or non-numeric results for WQS-linked parameters are classified when evidence is incomplete (C).

candidates.exact_span: interim or final effluent limitations must be as stringent as those in the previous permit, unless material and substantial alterations or additions to the permitted facility occurred after permit issuance which justify the application of a less stringent effluent limitation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the antibacksliding exception applies could change which numeric limits are treated as enforceable when comparing proposed limits to prior-permit limits.

candidates.exact_span: The proposed permit is slightly more restrictive than the previous permit since the Cyanide limits have been established in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether newly established Cyanide limits are operative enforceable numeric limits could change whether reported cyanide measurements are subject to compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: In addition, the 30-day average TDS net incremental increase and loading limits have been revised downward to 449 mg/L (from 497 mg/L) and to 24,992 lbs/day (from 27,664 lbs/day), respectively, in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The stated TDS concentration and loading values are candidate enforceable numeric limits; different interpretation of which limit form applies could change exceedance determinations for TDS measurements.

candidates.exact_span: For other pollutants (i.e., BOD5, TSS, pH, E. coli, and TRC), their limits are kept the same.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether limits for these parameters are carried forward unchanged from the prior permit affects which numeric limits are deemed applicable for compliance comparison during FY2025.
